title: The Effect of Short-Term Rentals on Residential Investment
authors: Ron Bekkerman; Maxime C. Cohen; Edward Kung; John Maiden; Davide Proserpio
eligible_reason: Staggered binary adoption of short-term-rental (home-sharing) regulations at the zipcode level: regulation_time takes 13 distinct in-sample implementation months (plus 2 cohorts after the sample end and 59 never-regulated zipcodes). All DiD results in the package are Callaway-Sant'Anna att_gt estimates (idname=zipcode, tname=time, gname=regulation_time or passage_time, not-yet-treated controls, no covariates): simple ATT (Table 4) and dynamic event-study aggregations (Figures 1, 3, 4, 5, 6). No controls, weights or additional regressors. TWFE counterparts are not in the code and must be constructed. Project-member-authored paper (D. Proserpio), to be disclosed per PROTOCOL Section 6.
design_notes: Zipcode-month panel (755 zipcodes, months 72-215 = Jan 2008-Dec 2019, 90,682 rows, unbalanced). Treatment cohorts by regulation_time (zipcodes): 127 (48), 150 (32), 155 (29), 157 (31), 173 (59), 177 (100), 183 (26), 198 (31), 203 (40), 204 (53), 210 (70), 213 (97), 215 (22); 231 (16) and 246 (42) fall after the last sample month and are effectively never treated; 0 = never regulated (59). passage_time gives an alternative cohort structure (17 nonzero values). Border-discontinuity regressions in replbdd.R (Tables 6-8: felm(log(1+permits) ~ inside | bdum + YMO), cross-sectional border design) are not DiD and are excluded. Outcome variables are already log(1+x) transformed in the data file.
estimators_reported: border discontinuity felm with border-segment and year-month FE (Tables 6-8; not DiD)
n_adoption_cohorts_note: 13 in-sample implementation cohorts (regulation_time), 2 further cohorts after Dec 2019 (treated as never-treated by att_gt), 59 never-regulated zipcodes; passage_time definition has 15 in-sample cohorts.
modern_estimators_named: Callaway-Sant'Anna (R did::att_gt, aggte simple and dynamic)

specs.treatment_var: regulation_time (gname): month index (months since Jan 2002) in which the zipcode's short-term-rental regulation was implemented; 0 = never regulated. att_gt builds the binary treated indicator 1[time >= regulation_time].
specs.treatment_definition: binary, absorbing: zipcode is treated from the month its home-sharing ordinance/short-term-rental regulation took effect (regulation_time), never-treated zipcodes coded 0; alternative definition uses passage_time (month the regulation was passed)
specs.fe: CSA group-time ATTs (equivalent to zipcode + month FE); control_group = 'notyettreated'; allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE; bstrap = TRUE
specs.cluster: zipcode (default att_gt clustering by idname, bootstrap)

data_access_detail: Final analysis datasets shipped as CSV (repldid.csv, replbdd.csv); zipcode-level aggregates of Airbnb listings and building permits.
software_detail: R: did (att_gt/aggte, installed from GitHub bcallaway11/did), lfe::felm, ggplot2
screener_notes: Package contains only CSA code; TWFE static and event-study counterparts can be constructed directly from repldid.csv (zipcode, time, regulation_time). Note att_gt uses control_group='notyettreated' and allow_unbalanced_panel=TRUE. Coauthored by project member Davide Proserpio.
